newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - few spot beans available.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - few spot beans available.

text.p: Tight supplies of spot coffee continued to dominate discussion on the New York physical market this week, with spreads on much sought-after beans holding firm, traders said.
Recent volatility on the futures market, coupled with CSCE December's hefty premium to second-position March, forced roasters with dwinding inventories to pay up for sorely needed coffee.
"Roasters are running out of coffee and are willing to pay substantial premiums," one trader said. "For spot coffee you can ask any price you want because there aren't any spots."
With European spot inventories also running low, traders said U.S. roasters were not only fighting internally for coffee but bidding against European roasters too.
"The U.S. and Europe are competiting, and they will outbid you," a trader said. "The bulk of the coffee is going to Europe."

Although Colombian coffee is expected to begin flowing into the market following the end last week of a 12-day truckers' strike, dealers said it was likely to be mid-November before deliveries get back to normal.
